intro: A small, sturdy companion with a flat face and famous upright "bat ears". Quiet and happy in a flat, which helps explain why it's the most popular breed in the US.
fun_fact: Most Frenchies can't swim well: their heavy front end and short muzzle make it hard to keep their head above water.

intro: A strong, medium-large retriever with a short, water-resistant coat in black, yellow or chocolate. Loves people, food and water in roughly that order.
fun_fact: Labs were bred from the St. John's water dogs that helped Newfoundland fishermen haul nets and fetch fish that slipped off the line.

intro: A gentle gun dog with a flowing golden coat, bred to retrieve shot birds from water and moorland. Famously good with children.
fun_fact: The breed was developed in the 1860s by Lord Tweedmouth at his Scottish estate, Guisachan, starting from a yellow retriever called Nous.

intro: A large, athletic herding dog with a noble outline and a sharp mind. Today it's a top choice for police, search-and-rescue and guide work.
fun_fact: Max von Stephanitz founded the breed in 1899 after buying a single dog he admired at a show, named Horand von Grafrath.

intro: The long, low "sausage dog" comes in smooth, wire and longhaired coats and in standard and miniature sizes. Big personality, big bark.
fun_fact: "Dachshund" means "badger dog" in German: the short legs and deep chest were made for digging into badger setts.

intro: Comes in standard, miniature and toy sizes, all with a dense, curly coat that sheds very little. One of the most intelligent breeds.
fun_fact: The fancy poodle clip started as a practical one for water work: shaved legs for swimming, with hair left to keep the joints and chest warm.

intro: A compact scent hound that hunts in packs and follows its nose everywhere. Its loud, baying howl is called a "bay".
fun_fact: Beagles work in airports for the US Department of Agriculture's "Beagle Brigade", sniffing luggage for forbidden food and plants.

intro: A powerful, black-and-tan working dog, calm and steady with its family and watchful with strangers.
fun_fact: Named after the town of Rottweil, where they drove cattle to market. The story goes that butchers tied their money pouches around the dogs' necks for safety.

intro: A versatile hunting dog with a short liver or liver-and-white coat. It points, retrieves and swims, and needs lots of exercise.
fun_fact: German hunters wanted one dog that could do everything, from tracking deer to fetching ducks, and bred the GSP to be that all-rounder.

intro: A low, wide, wrinkly dog with a pushed-in nose and a rolling walk. Despite the tough look, it's a gentle couch companion.
fun_fact: The Bulldog is a symbol of Britain's stubborn courage, and it's the mascot of many universities, including Yale's "Handsome Dan".

intro: A big, muscular Italian mastiff used to guard farms and hunt wild boar. Devoted to its people and serious about protecting them.
fun_fact: Its name is thought to come from Latin and roughly means "bodyguard dog". The breed nearly vanished in the 20th century before enthusiasts revived it in the 1970s.

intro: A small spaniel with long, silky ears and big, soft eyes. Happy to go for a walk or curl up on a lap.
fun_fact: King Charles II was so fond of these little spaniels that he was rarely seen without a few at his heels.

intro: A tiny terrier with a long, silky steel-blue and tan coat. A bossy little character in a toy-sized body.
fun_fact: Yorkies were bred to catch rats in Victorian mills and mines. A Yorkie called Smoky served with US troops in World War II.

intro: A medium herding dog with a striking coat that is often merle, and sometimes eyes of two colours. Needs a job and plenty of exercise.
fun_fact: Aussies were developed on ranches in the American West. The "Australian" probably comes from the Basque shepherds who brought sheep from Australia.

intro: A sleek, athletic guardian with a short black-and-rust coat. Loving with its family and very trainable.
fun_fact: A tax collector named Louis Dobermann created the breed in the 1890s to protect him on his rounds.

intro: A short-legged herding dog with a fox-like face and usually little or no tail. Quick, bold and full of fun.
fun_fact: Queen Elizabeth II owned more than 30 Pembroke Corgis over her lifetime.

intro: A small, sturdy terrier-type dog with a wiry coat, bushy eyebrows and a beard. A cheerful, alert companion.
fun_fact: "Schnauze" is German for "snout", a nod to the breed's moustached muzzle.

intro: A strong, square-built dog with a short coat and an underbite. Playful and bouncy well into adulthood.
fun_fact: One story for the name is the way Boxers rear up and bat at things with their front paws, like a boxer.

intro: A tiny spitz with a huge fluffy coat and a fox-like face. Confident, curious and quick to bark at visitors.
fun_fact: Early Pomeranians were much bigger. Queen Victoria fell for small ones and helped shrink the breed to toy size.

intro: A big, gentle farm dog with a long tricolour coat of black, rust and white. Loves cold weather and its family.
fun_fact: Bernese were used to pull small carts of milk and cheese to market in the canton of Bern.

intro: A small companion dog with a long, flowing coat and a sweet, upturned face. Bred to be a lap dog.
fun_fact: The name means "little lion" in Chinese, and they were treasured pets of the Chinese imperial court.

intro: A giant, elegant dog with a short coat. Despite its size, it's a gentle companion known as the "Apollo of dogs".
fun_fact: A Great Dane named Zeus holds the record for the tallest dog ever, at 1.12 m (44 in) at the shoulder.

intro: A compact, short-coated dog in a black-and-white "tuxedo" pattern. Lively, polite and easy to live with.
fun_fact: It's nicknamed the "American Gentleman" for that tuxedo coat, and it was one of the first breeds developed in the US.

intro: The smallest breed in the world, with either a smooth or long coat. Fiercely loyal to one or two people.
fun_fact: The breed is named after the Mexican state of Chihuahua, and probably descends from the ancient Techichi dogs of the Toltecs.

intro: A small, sturdy toy dog with a long, silky coat and a springy walk. Happiest wherever its people are.
fun_fact: The Havanese is Cuba's national dog. Almost every Havanese today descends from just 11 dogs brought to the US after the Cuban revolution.

intro: A medium herding dog with intense focus and endless energy. Often called the most intelligent breed.
fun_fact: A Border Collie named Chaser learned the names of more than 1,000 different toys.

intro: A medium gun dog with long ears and a liver-and-white or black-and-white coat. Bred to "spring" (flush) birds into the air for hunters.
fun_fact: Springers are favourites as detection dogs, sniffing out drugs and explosives at borders and airports.

intro: A smaller version of the Australian Shepherd, with the same striking coats and herding instincts in a more portable size.
fun_fact: These dogs were bred down from small Aussies in California in the 1960s, and were long known as "Miniature Australian Shepherds".

intro: A small herding dog that looks like a mini Rough Collie, with a long double coat. Sensitive and quick to learn.
fun_fact: On the Shetland Islands everything is small: ponies, sheep, and the sheepdogs that herded them.

intro: A medium sled dog with a thick coat, a curled tail and often blue or two-coloured eyes. Built to run long distances in the cold.
fun_fact: In 1925 husky teams relayed medicine 1,085 km (674 miles) to Nome, Alaska, to stop a diphtheria outbreak. The run inspired the Iditarod race.

intro: A medium, leggy bird dog with an orange-and-white or liver-and-white coat. Quick, eager and athletic.
fun_fact: The AKC dropped "Spaniel" from the name in 1982 because the Brittany hunts more like a pointer.

intro: A lean, fawn shepherd with a black mask, one of four Belgian shepherd types. Intense and very driven.
fun_fact: A Malinois named Cairo was part of the US Navy SEAL team on the 2011 mission to capture Osama bin Laden.

intro: The smallest sporting breed, with long ears, a domed head and a silky coat. Sweet-natured and merry.
fun_fact: A Cocker Spaniel named Checkers became famous in 1952 when Richard Nixon mentioned him in a TV speech, now called the "Checkers speech".

intro: A low, heavy-boned scent hound with long, droopy ears and a mournful face. Easygoing, but stubborn when on a scent.
fun_fact: After the Bloodhound, the Basset has one of the best noses of any dog. Its long ears help sweep scents up towards its nose.

intro: A medium gun dog, a little taller and longer in the head than the American Cocker. Bred to flush woodcock.
fun_fact: The name "cocker" comes from the woodcock, the bird these spaniels were bred to hunt.

intro: A sleek pointer with a short, golden-rust coat. Known as the "Velcro dog" because it sticks to its owner's side.
fun_fact: Vizslas were the hunting dogs of Hungarian nobility and the breed nearly died out after World War II.

intro: A tiny toy dog with a long, silky, pure white coat. Bred for thousands of years purely to be a companion.
fun_fact: Maltese-type dogs appear on ancient Greek pottery, making them one of the oldest toy breeds.

intro: A small, square dog with a wrinkled face, a curly tail and a big personality. A clown who loves company.
fun_fact: A group of pugs is called a "grumble". In 1572 a pug is said to have saved the life of William of Orange by raising the alarm.

intro: A large herding dog that comes in rough (long) and smooth coats. Gentle, loyal and quick to learn.
fun_fact: The famous film dog Lassie was a Rough Collie, though the role was usually played by male dogs.

intro: A giant guardian with a massive head and a short fawn or brindle coat. Calm and gentle with its family.
fun_fact: An English Mastiff named Zorba weighed 155.6 kg (343 lb) in 1989, one of the heaviest dogs ever recorded.

intro: A strong hound with a short wheaten coat and a ridge of hair along its back growing the wrong way.
fun_fact: Ridgebacks were known as "African lion hounds": packs kept lions at bay until the hunters arrived.

intro: A dainty toy spaniel with large, fringed ears that look like butterfly wings. Clever and quick.
fun_fact: "Papillon" is French for "butterfly". A version with droopy ears is called the Phalène, meaning "moth".

intro: A medium, muscular water dog with a curly or wavy coat. Bred to help fishermen.
fun_fact: These dogs herded fish into nets and carried messages between boats. Bo and Sunny lived in the White House with the Obamas.

intro: A small, foxy spitz with a red, sesame or black-and-tan coat and a curled tail. Clean and cat-like.
fun_fact: Shibas are famous for the "Shiba scream", a loud shriek when they're unhappy, and a Shiba called Kabosu became the "Doge" meme.

intro: A small, sturdy terrier with a stiff white coat and a carrot-shaped tail. Bold and cheerful.
fun_fact: Legend says Westies were bred white after a Scottish colonel accidentally shot his reddish terrier, mistaking it for a fox.

intro: A giant, heavy-coated water dog with webbed feet. Famous as a nanny dog and a lifesaver.
fun_fact: Newfoundlands have pulled drowning people from the water, and one is said to have saved Napoleon after he fell overboard.

intro: A compact, tough herding dog with a blue or red speckled coat. Tireless and very loyal.
fun_fact: An Australian Cattle Dog named Bluey lived 29 years and 5 months, one of the oldest dogs ever recorded.

intro: A medium sighthound that looks like a small Greyhound. Couch potato at home, lightning-fast outside.
fun_fact: Whippets can reach about 56 km/h (35 mph), and were nicknamed the "poor man's racehorse" in northern England.

intro: A small, cheerful dog with a soft, curly white coat and dark eyes. Sheds very little.
fun_fact: Bichons were popular with French and Spanish nobility, and later performed tricks in circuses and on street corners.

intro: A sleek, athletic dog with a white coat covered in black or liver spots. Bred to run alongside carriages.
fun_fact: Dalmatian puppies are born pure white; their spots appear over the first couple of weeks.

intro: A medium gun dog with a harsh, wiry coat and a bearded face. Hunts close and retrieves on land and water.
fun_fact: The breed was developed in the 1870s by a Dutchman, Eduard Korthals, so in Europe it's called the Korthals Griffon.

intro: The largest of the three schnauzers, with a black or salt-and-pepper wiry coat. Powerful and protective.
fun_fact: Bavarian farmers bred Giant Schnauzers to drive cattle, and later they worked as guard dogs at breweries and butcher shops.

intro: The smallest sighthound, a slender, elegant dog with a short, silky coat. Sweet and sensitive.
fun_fact: Frederick the Great of Prussia adored them, and he is buried beside his dogs at his palace of Sanssouci.

intro: A large, sleek gun dog with a short silver-grey coat and light eyes. Energetic and people-loving.
fun_fact: It's nicknamed the "grey ghost" for its silvery coat and silent hunting style. Photographer William Wegman made Weimaraners art stars.

intro: A fluffy white spitz with a thick coat and a famous "Sammy smile" (upturned lips). Loves people and cold weather.
fun_fact: The Samoyede people of Siberia used these dogs to herd reindeer and pull sleds, and slept beside them for warmth.

intro: A strong water retriever with an oily, wavy coat that sheds water. Tough enough for icy waves.
fun_fact: The breed descends from two Newfoundland puppies rescued from a sinking ship off Maryland in 1807.

intro: A short-legged terrier with a wiry coat, a beard and big eyebrows. Dignified and a bit stubborn.
fun_fact: President Franklin D. Roosevelt's Scottie, Fala, was so famous that he has a statue at the FDR Memorial in Washington.

intro: A versatile hunting dog with a weatherproof wiry coat and a bearded face. Hardworking and loyal.
fun_fact: Its wiry coat sheds water and protects the dog from thorny bushes while hunting.

intro: A large scent hound with long ears, droopy skin and a very keen nose. Patient and gentle.
fun_fact: A Bloodhound's evidence can be accepted in some US courts. One named Nick Carter tracked a trail that was 105 hours old.

intro: A small, tough terrier with a short-legged, rectangular build. Bred to chase foxes out of their dens.
fun_fact: The breed is named after Parson John Russell, a 19th-century English clergyman who loved fox hunting.

intro: A medium, muscular terrier with a short coat and a broad head. Loving and loyal with people.
fun_fact: In the UK, Staffies have been nicknamed the "nanny dog" for their affection for children.

intro: A large, powerful spitz with a curled tail and a thick coat. Quiet and very loyal to its family.
fun_fact: Hachikō, an Akita, waited for his owner at Tokyo's Shibuya station every day for nearly 10 years after the man died. A statue marks the spot.

intro: A giant, gentle dog with a short or long coat. Calm, patient and friendly.
fun_fact: Monks at the Great St Bernard Pass used these dogs to find travellers lost in the snow. A dog called Barry is credited with saving more than 40 people.

intro: A medium spaniel with a wavy chocolate coat. Bred to hunt ducks and turkeys from small boats.
fun_fact: The Boykin is the official state dog of South Carolina.

intro: A low herding dog with a long, fox-like tail and big rounded ears. The older of the two corgi breeds.
fun_fact: Cardigans have been herding cattle in Wales for more than 3,000 years, according to breed tradition.

intro: A large, majestic livestock guardian with a thick white coat. Calm but fearless.
fun_fact: Great Pyrenees have double dewclaws on their back legs, which may help them grip rough mountain ground.

intro: A small, sleek dog with a high-stepping "hackney" walk. Confident and full of energy.
fun_fact: It looks like a mini Doberman, but the Min Pin is the older breed and isn't related to the Doberman at all.

intro: A small, shaggy working terrier with a weather-resistant coat. Curious and confident.
fun_fact: Toto in the 1939 film The Wizard of Oz was a female Cairn Terrier named Terry.

intro: The smallest retriever, with a red coat and white markings. Playful and full of energy.
fun_fact: Tollers lure ducks closer by playing on the shore, a trick foxes also use to tempt curious birds.

intro: The largest terrier, with a wiry black-and-tan coat. Called the "King of Terriers".
fun_fact: Airedales carried messages and supplies across the battlefields of World War I.

intro: A large, sturdy, tricolour working dog with a short coat. Gentle and loves to be with people.
fun_fact: It's the oldest and largest of the four Swiss mountain dog breeds and was once nicknamed the "poor man's horse".

intro: A small, elegant dog that is either hairless with silky tufts or fully coated (the "Powderpuff").
fun_fact: Both hairless and Powderpuff puppies can be born in the same litter.

intro: A tall, elegant bird dog with a glossy red coat. Playful and full of energy.
fun_fact: Irish Setters were originally red-and-white. The solid red coat became popular in the 19th century.

intro: A toy terrier with a long, silky coat in white, black and tan. A cheerful, gentle companion.
fun_fact: The breed began in 1984 with a single puppy born to Yorkshire Terriers owned by Werner and Gertrud Biewer.

intro: The tallest of all dog breeds, with a rough coat and a gentle nature. Bred to hunt wolves.
fun_fact: An old Irish saying describes the Wolfhound as "gentle when stroked, fierce when provoked".

intro: A medium terrier with a soft, silky coat the colour of ripening wheat. Cheerful and bouncy.
fun_fact: Wheaten puppies are born dark and their coats lighten to wheat colour over the first two years.

intro: A medium dog with a thick, curly coat. Originally a water retriever, it's now a truffle hunter.
fun_fact: The Lagotto is the only breed recognised as a specialist truffle hunter.

intro: A large, powerful guardian with a short coat and a black mask. Calm and loving with its family.
fun_fact: Gamekeepers bred Bullmastiffs to pin poachers down without mauling them, earning the name "gamekeeper's night dog".

intro: A small, cheerful dog with a soft, cottony white coat. Loves company.
fun_fact: It's the national dog of Madagascar. "Coton" is French for "cotton" and Tulear is a port town on the island.

intro: A medium dog with deep wrinkles, a blue-black tongue and a short, bristly coat.
fun_fact: Shar-Pei means "sand skin" in Chinese, for the rough feel of their coat.

intro: A large, powerful sled dog with a thick coat and a plumed tail. Built for strength, not speed.
fun_fact: Malamutes are named after the Mahlemut people of Alaska and were used to haul heavy loads, even on polar expeditions.

intro: A small toy dog with a bearded, almost human face. Bold and full of character.
fun_fact: Griffons were kept by Brussels coachmen to catch rats in stables. A griffon co-starred in the film As Good as It Gets.

intro: A small dog with a long, heavy coat. Bred as a watchdog in Tibetan monasteries.
fun_fact: Lhasa Apsos were seen as sacred and were given as gifts by the Dalai Lama.

intro: A small, muscular terrier with a short coat. Quick, clever and great at pest control.
fun_fact: President Theodore Roosevelt is said to have named the breed after his dogs cleared rats from the White House.

intro: A medium spitz with a thick grey and black coat and dark "spectacles" around its eyes.
fun_fact: The Keeshond became a symbol of the Dutch Patriot party in the 18th century, named after its leader Cornelis (Kees) de Gyselaer.

intro: A muscular terrier with a unique egg-shaped head. Fun-loving and full of energy.
fun_fact: A Bull Terrier named Bullseye was the long-time mascot of the US retailer Target.

intro: A large, shaggy herding dog with a profuse grey-and-white coat that often covers its eyes. Playful and loving.
fun_fact: Old English Sheepdogs were bred to drive cattle and sheep to market in south-west England.

intro: A large, rugged livestock guardian with a short or rough coat. Calm and protective.
fun_fact: In Namibia, Anatolians guard livestock from cheetahs, helping protect the big cats from farmers too.

intro: An elegant bird dog with a speckled coat known as "belton". Gentle and sweet.
fun_fact: "Belton" comes from a village in Northumberland where the breed's founder, Edward Laverack, liked to hunt.

intro: A small, lion-like toy dog with a long, flowing coat and a flat face. Dignified and confident.
fun_fact: Pekingese were kept by the Chinese imperial family. Legend says stealing one was punishable by death.

intro: A small terrier with an otter-shaped head and a wiry coat. Good-natured and hardworking.
fun_fact: Borders were bred to keep pace with horses on fox hunts and then go to ground after the fox.

intro: A small, elegant hunting dog with a curled tail and wrinkled forehead. Clean and cat-like.
fun_fact: The Basenji doesn't bark. Instead it makes a yodelling sound called a "baroo".

intro: The original schnauzer, a medium dog with a wiry coat, beard and eyebrows. Clever and spirited.
fun_fact: The Standard Schnauzer is the oldest of the three schnauzer breeds; the miniature and giant were developed from it.

intro: A medium, lion-like spitz with a thick coat and a blue-black tongue. Independent and reserved.
fun_fact: Chows walk with a stiff, stilted gait because their back legs are very straight.

intro: A large, powerful mastiff with a huge head and a short fawn coat. Calm and devoted.
fun_fact: A Dogue de Bordeaux named Beasley co-starred with Tom Hanks in the 1989 film Turner & Hooch.

intro: A giant, lion-like dog with a long, water-resistant coat. Calm and great with families.
fun_fact: A mayor of Leonberg bred them to look like the lion on the town's coat of arms.

intro: A medium, stocky terrier with a short coat. Courageous and loving with its people.
fun_fact: The AKC first recognised the breed in 1936 as the Staffordshire Terrier, and added "American" to the name in 1972.

intro: A sleek retriever with a shiny black or liver coat. Cheerful and playful into old age.
fun_fact: Flat-Coats are known as the "Peter Pan" of dogs because they stay puppy-like for so long.

intro: A tall, elegant sighthound with a silky coat and a long, narrow head. Calm and gentle.
fun_fact: Russian nobility used Borzois to hunt wolves, and the breed was once called the Russian Wolfhound.

intro: A large, rugged herding dog with a shaggy coat and a beard. Calm and protective.
fun_fact: Bouviers served as messenger and ambulance dogs in World War I; the breed nearly died out in the war.
